    Theorem 5.2: the embedding theorem #

    An EmbeddingData k A collects what the manuscript establishes for each of the functors F_ν : D → Mod A of (3.5), apart from the reduction of Lemma 3.1: F is k-linear, faithful and exact on D, has finite-dimensional values on D_fin, satisfies the colimit comparison (3.6), admits retractions on C with a nilpotence bound (Proposition 4.8), and satisfies the two facts about S₋ that the proof of Theorem 5.2 takes from the representation-embedding property on D_fin: F(S₋) is indecomposable and not isomorphic to F(T) for T ∈ C_fin.

    Theorem 5.2 (EmbeddingData.theoremA_conclusion): such an F is a representation embedding on D with the three properties of Theorem A. The proof follows the manuscript.

    • Step 1 (noSummand): for T₀ ∈ C, F(T₀) has no direct summand isomorphic to P = F(S₋). A split monomorphism P → F(T₀) factors through F(T₁) for a finite-dimensional T₁ ⊆ T₀ in C, by (3.6). Instead of the Krull–Schmidt theorem we use the retractions: the idempotent of F(T₁) splitting off P is conjugate to F(η) for the idempotent η = ρ(ε) of T₁, so P is isomorphic to F of a summand of T₁ in C_fin.
    • Step 2 (reflects_iso): cancellation of the copies of P, by Lemma 5.1 and the block computation (5.1).
    • Step 3: preservation of indecomposability, by Lemma 2.4 on C and the fact that F(S₋) is indecomposable.

    The embedding transports along the functor of Lemma 3.1 (transport).
